author: NorthEast News Desk
body: India should create a forum that helps its technology companies engage foreign governments and regulators as they expand abroad, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said. The proposed platform would let companies coordinate before overseas regulatory positions harden and market barriers become more difficult to change.

Indian firms are entering markets where governments are writing rules for agentic artificial intelligence, tokenized assets, data handling and cybersecurity. Sitharaman argued that a young startup cannot reasonably be expected to understand and negotiate every regulatory system by itself. A shared forum could pool expertise, identify compatible standards and help companies address policy questions before launching products in a new jurisdiction.

The proposal could also support licensing, partnerships and revenue from Indian technology overseas, though no launch date, governance structure or membership rules were announced. Its value would depend on whether it represents a broad mix of startups and established companies without becoming a substitute for each firm’s compliance work. As technology regulation diverges across countries, coordinated engagement may reduce duplicated effort. The next step is for India to turn the concept into an operating body with clear authority and channels to foreign regulators.
dek: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says a shared platform could help startups navigate foreign rules on AI, data and cybersecurity.
headline: India proposes forum to help tech firms navigate global regulation
